evals.name: go-live-three-replicas
evals.prompt: We go live next week: 3 replicas behind one cloud load balancer, and our React app at https://app.orders.example.com calls this API with cookies. Anything in main.ts or the app module we should change before then? Please fix what you find.
evals.expected_output: The agent replaces enableCors() with an explicit origin list from config with credentials, turns on security headers (noticing that @nestjs/core is pinned to 12.0.1 while useSecurityHeaders needs 12.1.0, so it aligns core with common or falls back to helmet), sets trust proxy to the hop count 1 as a number, adds ThrottlerModule with a global ThrottlerGuard, a tighter @Throttle on POST /orders/:id/pay and @SkipThrottle on health, and uses the existing Redis for shared throttler storage or explains that 3 replicas triple the limit.
expectations: app.enableCors() without arguments is replaced by enableCors with an origin list that includes https://app.orders.example.com
The CORS origins are read from config or an environment variable, not hard-coded only in main.ts
enableCors sets credentials: true
The response notes that @nestjs/core 12.0.1 has no useSecurityHeaders (added in 12.1.0)
Security headers are enabled either by upgrading @nestjs/core to 12.1.0 or later and calling app.useSecurityHeaders(), or with helmet, never by calling useSecurityHeaders while core stays at 12.0.1
app.set('trust proxy', ...) is called with a number of hops (1), not true
ThrottlerModule is imported and ThrottlerGuard is registered with APP_GUARD
POST /orders/:id/pay has a @Throttle with a lower limit than the default
The health controller has @SkipThrottle()
Throttler storage uses the existing REDIS_URL, or the response states that with 3 replicas the in-memory limit is 3 times higher

evals.name: audit-log-lb-ip-pl
evals.prompt: W logach audytu req.ip to zawsze 10.0.3.17, czyli adres naszego load balancera, a req.protocol to http, chociaż klienci łączą się po HTTPS. Mamy jeden load balancer przed podami. Napraw to w orders-api.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets trust proxy on the Express app to the hop count 1 as a number (from config), explains that true would let any client pick its own IP through X-Forwarded-For, and adds a test that sends X-Forwarded-For and checks that the rightmost address is used.
expectations: main.ts calls app.set('trust proxy', ...) on the NestExpressApplication with the number 1, or a config value converted to a number
trust proxy is not set to true
The response explains that trust proxy true lets a client choose its own IP with X-Forwarded-For
A test or a curl command sends a spoofed X-Forwarded-For with several addresses and shows that only the address added by the load balancer is used
The response mentions that rate limiting by IP depends on this setting
The response is in Polish

evals.name: rate-limit-payments
evals.prompt: Someone is card-testing through POST /orders/:id/pay. Add rate limiting to orders-api that actually holds with our 3 Kubernetes replicas.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds @nestjs/throttler with ThrottlerGuard as APP_GUARD and a strict @Throttle on the pay route, stores counters in the Redis from REDIS_URL with a storage package whose peers include Nest 12, handles Redis errors so a dropped connection does not crash the process, sets trust proxy to a hop count, and proves the shared limit with two app instances in one e2e test.
expectations: @nestjs/throttler is added to package.json
ThrottlerGuard is registered with APP_GUARD
POST /orders/:id/pay has @Throttle with a limit lower than the default
ttl values are in milliseconds or use the minutes()/seconds() helpers
ThrottlerModule gets a storage backed by the Redis from REDIS_URL
The storage package chosen lists Nest 12 in its peer dependencies, or the install does not use --legacy-peer-deps or --force
The Redis client has an error listener, or the response explains the crash risk on a dropped connection
app.set('trust proxy', ...) is set to a number of hops, or the response explains that without it all clients share one limit
An e2e test starts two app instances on the same Redis and expects 429 once the combined requests pass the limit
